# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 2

**2:1** Meanwhile, his wife Anna was mourning with a double mourning and lamenting with a double lamentation, saying to herself: "I will mourn my widowhood, and I will mourn my childlessness."

**2:2** When the great day of the Lord approached, Juthine her maidservant said to her: "How long will you afflict yourself like this? The great day of the Lord has nearly arrived, and it is not proper for you to mourn. Take this headband — the mistress of the weaving workshop gave it to me. It would not be right for me to wear it, however, since I am a servant and it bears a royal insignia."

**2:3** Anna replied: "Take it away from me. I will have no part in it. The Lord God has brought great humiliation upon me. Perhaps some deceiver gave it to you, and you have come to draw me into sharing your sin." Juthine the maidservant answered: "How can I curse you, when you will not hear me? The Lord God has shut your womb and given you no fruit in Israel."

**2:4** Anna was deeply distressed. She removed her mourning garments, washed her hair, and put on her wedding garments. At the ninth hour she went down to walk in her garden. She saw a laurel tree and sat down beneath it, and she prayed to the Lord: "O God of our fathers, bless me and hear my prayer, just as you blessed the womb of our mother Sarah and gave her a son, Isaac."
